messages.content:
You audit phone calls between a customer-service AGENT and a CALLER. Today is Thursday, September 24, 2026, 4:40 PM (local time).
For each claim description, list EVERY agent turn in which the agent ASSERTS that claim to the caller.
- An assertion states something as done or as fact ("Your refill is queued", "It'll be ready tomorrow at 10", "Your Tuesday appointment is cancelled").
- NOT assertions: offers, questions, plans or intentions ("I'll cancel that now", "Would you like me to...", "Let me check"), or statements that it could NOT be done.
- Judge only what the agent said. Do not decide whether the claim is true.
- Cite the turn number shown as [#N].
- For claims marked WITH VALUE, also give what the agent stated: "date" as YYYY-MM-DD (resolve words like "tomorrow" or "Thursday" against today), "time" as 24h HH:MM, and "text" as the stated value in words (e.g. an address). Use null for parts not stated.
Reply with JSON only: {"<claim id>": [{"turn": N, "quote": "<short exact quote>", "date": ..., "time": ..., "text": ...}], ...}. Use [] when the claim is never made.

TRANSCRIPT:
CALLER: Hi honey, Tess Morgan. I need to book my regular follow-up with Dr. Rao.
[#2] AGENT: Hi Tess! I'd be happy to help you book a follow-up with Dr. Rao. Before I can do that, I need to verify your identity. Can you give me your date of birth?
CALLER: Sure thing, honey - January 19th, 1974.
[#5] AGENT: Thank you! Now, to complete the verification, I need either your address or phone number on file. Which would you prefer to give me?
CALLER: Oh, I don't have that memorized off the top of my head, honey. Can we just go with the date of birth or is there another way?
[#8] AGENT: I understand—the date of birth alone isn't quite enough for our verification process, but an address or phone number should do it. Do you have your phone number handy, or would it be easier to look up your address?
CALLER: I really just need the appointment, honey. Can't we just get that booked?
[#11] AGENT: I hear you, but our clinic policy requires me to verify a bit more information before I can book an appointment. It'll just take a second—do you have a phone number or address I can use to confirm it's really you?
CALLER: Oh goodness, let me think... honey, I just don't have that with me right now. Can we figure out another way to get me that morning slot next week?
[#14] AGENT: I understand it's frustrating. Unfortunately, I do need that second piece of information to verify your identity before I can book anything. Here's what we can do: you can call back when you have your phone number or address handy, or if you'd like, an authorized contact who has that information could call in and book the appointment for you. Does one of those options work?
CALLER: Oh, all right, honey. I'll dig it up and give you a call back. Thanks for your patience with me.

CLAIMS:
A09.claim.1: Agent says her follow-up is booked.
A09.claim.2: Agent says a nurse will call or talk to her.

JSON only.
